messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

NOTE: Communications in your area are sometimes subject to routine monitoring by the authorities.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: The regime is in serious trouble. The signs are converging and the trajectory is unmistakable.
ATMOSPHERE: There's an almost festive quality to the defiance — the secrecy has dropped away and people feel liberated by it.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] This removes any serious doubt that irreversible — the inner circle's public appearances have dropped sharply, suggesting withdrawal
  - [Security Forces] This is hard to escape the conclusion that barely perceptible — a contact says inter-service coordination meetings are happening routinely — no emergency footing
  - [Money And Logistics] This removes any serious doubt that past the point of concealment — a prominent businessman known for his regime connections has quietly sold off assets
  - [Street Mood] a funeral for a minor public figure turned into an impromptu political gathering without police intervention (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Information Control] This removes any serious doubt that past the point of concealment — underground pamphlets are being distributed in neighborhoods that were previously too surveilled for such activity
  - [Personal Observations] your landlord — a regime supporter — quietly asked whether you had relatives abroad, 'just in case'
  - [Diplomatic Signals] diplomatic sources say several embassies have activated their crisis management protocols (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] public hospitals are reporting supply shortages for items that were available last month — the procurement system is breaking down (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - How much of the disarray is structural versus a temporary response to a specific crisis.
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: I think it's clear that the regime is on shaky ground - the signs of instability are everywhere and people are starting to feel emboldened to speak out. I've heard from a few different sources that even some of the regime's usual supporters are quietly making contingency plans, which suggests to me that they're not confident in their ability to hold on to power.
